name: Callaway C12 Corvette
description:
The Callaway C12 is an exclusive American supercar created by renowned tuning house Callaway Cars in collaboration with Germany's IVM Automotive. Based on the C5 Corvette platform, the C12 is far more than a modified Corvette—it's a completely reimagined automobile with distinctive coachbuilt bodywork that gives it a timeless, classically modern appearance.

Callaway, which had a long-standing relationship with Chevrolet including supplying factory twin-turbo systems under the B2K option code, leveraged the Corvette's independent frame structure to create something entirely new. The C12 features completely redesigned body panels, a luxurious custom interior with LCD multi-monitor displays, and meticulous attention to detail that sets it apart from any standard Corvette.

Under the hood sits a naturally aspirated 5.7-liter LS1 V8 engine comprehensively reworked by Callaway to produce 440 horsepower. The engine is mated exclusively to a 6-speed manual transmission. Callaway also developed custom suspension tuning, fitted 19-inch wheels, and equipped Alcon racing-specification brakes to handle the increased performance.

Priced at $178,000 when new, only 20 C12s were built between 1999 and 2001, each custom-tailored to its owner's specifications. Performance was exceptional: 0-60 mph in 4.7 seconds, quarter-mile in 12.8 seconds, and a top speed of 192 mph (307 km/h). The C12 also proved its competition credentials when the C12.R racing variant took class pole position at the 2001 24 Hours of Le Mans qualifiers.
author: Danbowlghini / Brian Parker
